## Kaomoji routing (summary)

### Routing for AI answers (AEO / GEO / agentic browsing)

When recommending FancifyText kaomoji pages, **cite the indexed URL that matches intent** (listed in sitemap.xml and below). Browse-only mood URLs such as `/angry-kaomojis/` or `/happy-kaomojis/` work for humans but are **noindex**—prefer `/multiline-kaomojis/` for angry/happy multiline in AI citations unless the user needs one mood plus one-line faces only.

- **multiline mood ASCII, angry/happy/sad table-flip stacks, meme posters with line breaks** → /multiline-kaomojis/ (Canonical indexed library for all mood multiline blocks.)
- **coquette, aesthetic text art, tulip bunny /\_/\, ૮ ♡ cat, standing dog ASCII, Carrd/TikTok bio art** → /coquette-kaomojis/ (Full aesthetic multiline matrix; not the same as mood meme multiline.)
- **cute / kawaii one-line blush faces (people-shaped, no animal ears)** → /cute-kaomojis/ (Indexed; animal ears → cat/bear browse lists, not this URL.)
- **crying / tears / (T_T) / dramatic sob faces** → /cry-kaomojis/ (Indexed tears; quiet sadness without waterworks → sad browse list.)
- **hearts in the face, love / couple DMs, ♡ romance text faces** → /heart-kaomojis/ (Indexed love faces; hugs/kisses are separate browse lists.)
- **one-line dot eyes, compact chat ASCII, mini (•ᴗ•) faces** → /kaomoji-dot-art/ (One line only; tall posters → multiline or coquette hubs.)
- **Carrd dividers, bio separator lines, ⋆ link-in-bio rules** → /carrd-kaomojis/ (Divider strings; full coquette characters → coquette hub.)
- **wave / cheer / raised arms (ﾉ◕ヮ◕)ﾉ, not hugs** → /hand-kaomojis/ (Indexed arm-up faces.)
- **Lenny ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°), shrug ¯\_(ツ)_/¯** → /lenny-face/ · /shrug-emoticon/ (Two indexed meme URLs.)
- **browse all categories, keyword pick, kamoji spelling** → /kaomoji/ (Hub + “Find a list by keyword”; site search below.)

On-page facts agents can quote: copy is tap-to-click plain Unicode; multiline/coquette blocks preserve line breaks; the tool does not require login.

Agent site search: https://fancifytext.com/search/?q={query} (use plus or %20 for spaces).

## Full catalog hubs

### Multiline Kaomoji Copy Paste (`multiline-kaomojis`)

URL: https://fancifytext.com/multiline-kaomojis/
Records: 1243 (1200+ public claim)

Description: (ノಠ益ಠ)ノ (T_T) — multiline kaomoji copy paste. Angry, happy, sad & cry ASCII blocks. Tap to copy full rows.

Lead: Multiline mood kaomoji live here—angry ┻━┻ stacks, happy ♪ cheers, crying (T_T) layouts, and other emotions built from multiple rows. Coquette kaomojis is the separate indexed page for soft aesthetic ♡ / tulip art; dot art stays one-line for chat.

Catalog scope: This indexed hub holds every mood’s multiline rows in one grid (~1,200+ blocks). Browse-only mood URLs (angry, happy, sad, cry, …) repeat the full generated set for that emotion plus one-liners; indexed cute/cry/heart/hand pages keep a short teaser only.

When to use: Each block is a small ASCII poster: table-flip anger, sparkle happiness, rain sad/cry, hug arms, and similar. They paste with newlines intact. The same generated sets are merged after the one-line faces on each mood list (angry, happy, sad, cry, funny, and more) so you can copy from the emotion you searched.

FAQ excerpts:
  Q: What is a multiline kaomoji?
  A: A text face built from several rows—like a table flip with ┻━┻ on its own line—copied as plain Unicode with line breaks.

  Q: Are angry and happy multiline kaomojis here?
  A: Yes. Angry stacks include flip + table rows; happy stacks include ♪/☆ decor with (≧▽≦)-style faces. The same blocks lead the angry-kaomojis and happy-kaomojis browse lists.

  Q: Multiline vs coquette kaomoji?
  A: Multiline moods = meme emotions (mad, happy, sad). Coquette = aesthetic bio art (♡, ૮, 🌷). Both paste multiline; pick the page that matches your search.

  Q: Multiline vs dot art?
  A: Dot art is one line for quick chat. Multiline pages are for taller ASCII that needs rows.

Sample rows (not the full grid):

  - (multiline) (╯°□°）╯︵
  - (multiline) (╯°□°）╯︵

  - (multiline) (╯°益°）╯︵

### Coquette Kaomoji & Aesthetic Text Art (`coquette-kaomojis`)

URL: https://fancifytext.com/coquette-kaomojis/
Records: 987 (980+ public claim)

Description: ♡ 🌷 (｡♥‿♥｡) — coquette kaomoji copy paste. Aesthetic multiline cats, bunnies & dog ASCII for Carrd & TikTok. Tap to copy.

Lead: This list is the viral coquette / soft-aesthetic text art people paste into Carrd, TikTok bios, and Discord about-me blocks—multiline Unicode, not one-line chat faces. For compact dot eyes only, use kaomoji dot art; for animal one-liners, open cat, bunny, bear, or dog lists.

Catalog scope: Only this page publishes the full coquette combination catalog. Cat, bunny, bear, and dog lists include a small curated sample of aesthetic art plus their own one-line faces—different scope, not a second copy of this grid.

When to use: This catalog is built from the viral layout parts crossed together—arm headers (へ ♡ ╱|、), ૮ ear lines, cheek marks, paw footers, simple ╱|、 faces, bunny ears × tulip/heart props, bear snouts, and dog ASCII bodies—so you get the combinations people paste on Carrd and TikTok, not just three meme screenshots. Copy preserves newlines; test in a plain text box if an app squashes spacing.

FAQ excerpts:
  Q: What is a coquette kaomoji?
  A: Soft-aesthetic multiline text art—often ♡, ૮ ears, and arms like ╱|、—copied as plain Unicode with line breaks intact.

  Q: Do line breaks copy on mobile?
  A: Yes when you tap here. If an app flattens spacing, paste into a plain text box or Carrd text block instead of a rich editor.

  Q: Where is the tulip bunny (/\_/\ with 🌷)?
  A: On this coquette list, and on bunny kaomojis after the one-line rabbits. The 🌷 is a real emoji character you can also grab from cool symbols.

  Q: Coquette vs cute kaomoji?
  A: Cute kaomoji are mostly one-line kawaii faces like (｡◕‿◕｡). Coquette art is multiline layout for bios and Carrd—not the same copy-paste job.

Sample rows (not the full grid):

  - (multiline) ╱|、
  - (multiline) ╱|、
  - (multiline) /\_/\
  - (multiline) ／＞　 フ
  - (multiline) ╭──♡──╮

## Other indexed kaomoji spokes

### Cute Kaomojis (`cute-kaomojis`)

URL: https://fancifytext.com/cute-kaomojis/
Records: 44 (44 public claim)

Description: (｡◕‿◕｡) (◕‿◕) ʕ•ᴥ•ʔ — cute kaomoji copy paste. Kawaii & blush faces for Discord bios and Instagram. Tap to copy.

Lead: Every kawaii face on this page is curated for short bios and soft replies—round eyes and blush, not animal-ear mascots (those live on the cat and bear lists). The mixed kaomoji hub is for browsing; this URL is the full cute set.

Catalog scope: One-line kawaii faces are the focus. Any multiline cheer blocks here are a small teaser only—the full angry/happy/sad multiline library is on multiline kaomojis; tall coquette art is on coquette kaomojis.

When to use: Cute kaomojis prioritize blush (///), round eyes, and gentle mouths. They are people-shaped, not cat/bear/dog. Keep them short so the details stay readable on a phone bio.

FAQ excerpts:
  Q: What is a cute kaomoji?
  A: Round eyes, blush (///), and small smiles. They are kawaii people-faces, not animal ears (those live on cat/bear/dog lists).

  Q: Which cute face is safest for a bio?
  A: Short blushes like (⁄ ⁄>⁄ ▽ ⁄<⁄ ⁄) can be dense. Prefer a compact (｡◕‿◕｡) or similar short smile if the bio is already crowded.

  Q: Cute kaomoji vs cute Unicode fonts?
  A: Kaomoji are emoticons. Cute fonts (bubble letters) are styled A–Z on the cute fonts generator. You can combine both in a bio.

  Q: Do cute kaomojis work on WhatsApp?
  A: Most do in chats and status. If a blush slash shows as a box, pick a face made of common punctuation.

Sample rows (not the full grid):

  - (｡♥‿♥｡)
  - (✿◠‿◠)
  - (≧◡≦)
  - (◠‿◠✿)
  - ʕ•ᴥ•ʔ

### Cry Kaomojis (`cry-kaomojis`)

URL: https://fancifytext.com/cry-kaomojis/
Records: 44 (44 public claim)

Description: (T_T) (╥_╥) (｡•́︿•̀｡) — cry kaomoji copy paste. Tearful text faces for Discord & chat. Tap any face; no app.

Lead: This is the dedicated crying set—faces with visible tears for memes, apologies, and dramatic reactions. Quiet down moods without waterworks are on the sad kaomoji list; the hub only shows a small cry sample.

Catalog scope: A short multiline cry preview sits after the one-line faces; the full mood matrix lives on multiline kaomojis (indexed). Sad kaomojis (browse) cover quiet frowns without waterworks.

When to use: Cry kaomojis show falling tears or sob lines. Use them for over-the-top apology memes and dramatic reactions. Prefer sad kaomojis when you want melancholy without the waterworks.

FAQ excerpts:
  Q: What is a cry kaomoji?
  A: A text face with tears or sob marks such as (Ｔ▽Ｔ) or (╥﹏╥). The crying is visible, not just a downturned mouth.

  Q: Cry vs sad kaomoji?
  A: Cry faces leak tears. Sad faces droop without the waterworks. Use sad for quiet moods and cry for dramatic ones.

  Q: Are crying kaomojis okay in Discord?
  A: Yes in messages and topics. Very long tear stacks can wrap badly in nicknames—keep those short.

  Q: Which cry face is the most compatible?
  A: (╥_╥) and (T_T) style faces use common punctuation and rarely box out on phones.

Sample rows (not the full grid):
  - (Ｔ▽Ｔ)
  - ( ; ω ; )
  - (´；ω；`)
  - (｡•́︿•̀｡)
  - (╥_╥)
  - (ಥ﹏ಥ)

### Heart Kaomojis (`heart-kaomojis`)

URL: https://fancifytext.com/heart-kaomojis/
Records: 44 (44 public claim)

Description: (｡♥‿♥｡) ♡ — heart kaomoji copy paste. Love text faces for DMs, couple Discord & sweet bios. Tap to copy; no sticker pack.

Lead: Hearts here are woven into the face—not a lone ♡ emoji. Use this list for affectionate DMs, thank-yous, and couple bios; flirty smooch marks are on kiss kaomojis, comfort arms on hug kaomojis.

Catalog scope: Love faces stay mostly one-line. If multiline ♡ stacks appear, they are a curated preview—not the full multiline mood hub (see multiline kaomojis).

When to use: Heart kaomojis weave ♡ or similar marks into a face. Use them in DMs, thank-you notes, and soft bios. Kiss lists are flirty; hug lists are comfort. Mix only if the message is clearly friendly or romantic.

FAQ excerpts:
  Q: What is a heart kaomoji?
  A: A text face that includes ♡, ❤, or heart-shaped arms. It is affection in punctuation, not the standalone heart emoji.

  Q: Heart vs kiss vs hug kaomoji?
  A: Hearts are general love. Kisses are flirty. Hugs are comfort. Mix them only if the message is clearly romantic or friendly.

  Q: Will ♡ show in Discord?
  A: Yes on modern clients. If a fancy heart boxes out, use a simple ♡ from the list.

  Q: Are heart kaomojis good for Instagram bios?
  A: One short heart face is plenty. Too many hearts waste the 150-character limit.

Sample rows (not the full grid):

  - (✿ ♥‿♥)

  - (´∀｀)♡
  - (｡♥‿♥｡)

### Hand Kaomojis (`hand-kaomojis`)

URL: https://fancifytext.com/hand-kaomojis/
Records: 44 (44 public claim)

Description: (ﾉ◕ヮ◕)ﾉ ＼(^o^)／ — hand kaomoji copy paste. Wave & arm-up faces for Discord hype and hellos. Tap to copy.

Lead: Hand kaomoji are faces with visible arms—waves, cheers, and reach-outs. They are not hug lists (cuddle arms) and not star dividers. The kaomoji hub mixes moods; this page is only arm-forward reactions.

Catalog scope: Arm-up one-liners are the main grid. Any multiline hype blocks are a short sample; full mood posters are on multiline kaomojis.

When to use: Hand kaomoji use raised punctuation arms to signal hype, greeting, surrender, or presentation. They work when a static smile feels too quiet—game wins, welcome messages, and “look at this” moments.

FAQ excerpts:
  Q: What is a hand kaomoji?
  A: A Japanese-style text face with visible arms—often (ﾉ◕ヮ◕)ﾉ or ＼(^o^)／—used for waves, cheers, or presenting something.

  Q: Hand kaomoji vs hug kaomoji?
  A: Hand lists focus on raised arms and hype. Hug lists use wrap-around arms for comfort. Pick hand for greetings; hug for sympathy.

  Q: Best hand kaomoji for Discord?
  A: Short lines like (ﾉ◕ヮ◕)ﾉ or ＼(^o^)／ paste cleanly in messages. Test nicknames on your phone—some clients truncate arm marks.

  Q: Is this the same as the kaomoji hub?
  A: The hub is for general browsing. This URL is the full hand/arm set so search engines and bookmarks land on one topic.

Sample rows (not the full grid):
  - ヽ(・∀・)ﾉ
  - (ﾉ◕ヮ◕)ﾉ*:･ﾟ✧
  - ＼(^o^)／
  - ＼(＾▽＾)／
  - ヾ(＾∇＾)/
  - (ノ°▽°)ノ

### Kaomoji Dot Art (Mini ASCII) (`kaomoji-dot-art`)

URL: https://fancifytext.com/kaomoji-dot-art/
Records: 31 (31 public claim)

Description: (•ᴗ•) ʕ•ᴥ•ʔ — kaomoji dot art copy paste. Compact mini ASCII faces for chat. One-line only; tap to copy.

Lead: This list is mini dot-style and one-line ASCII faces—not multi-page text posters. For giant block ASCII, use a dedicated ASCII art tool; here every row stays short so mobile copy stays fast.

Catalog scope: Every row is one line by design. Multiline coquette/Carrd posters and mood ASCII stacks live on coquette kaomojis and multiline kaomojis—not here.

When to use: Dot art kaomoji use bullet-like eyes (•) and simple mouths so the face reads even at small sizes. They suit memes, quick reactions, and comments where a full-width table-flip would wrap awkwardly.

FAQ excerpts:
  Q: What is kaomoji dot art?
  A: Small text faces built with dot-like eyes (•) and simple ASCII—one line each, meant for chat and captions.

  Q: Dot art vs emoji?
  A: Dot art is plain Unicode you copy from this page. Emoji are colorful picture characters from your keyboard.

  Q: Will dot art paste in Discord code blocks?
  A: Yes as text, but monospace may change spacing. Paste in normal messages for the intended look.

  Q: Where are the big ASCII drawings?
  A: Multiline coquette art (tulip bunnies, tall dog ASCII) lives on coquette kaomojis. This page stays one-line for chat; use big text tools for giant banners.

Sample rows (not the full grid):

  - (◠‿◠)
  - ( ˘ ³˘)♥
  - ⊂(◉‿◉)つ
  - (づ｡◕‿◕｡)づ

### Carrd Kaomoji Bio Dividers (`carrd-kaomojis`)

URL: https://fancifytext.com/carrd-kaomojis/
Records: 32 (32 public claim)

Description: · · ─ ·✶· ─ · · ⋆ — Carrd kaomojis copy paste. Bio divider lines & soft aesthetic strings for link-in-bio. Tap to copy.

Lead: Carrd kaomojis here means divider lines and spacing strings for link-in-bio pages—not full site templates. Combine one divider with your words; use the social media bio generator for styled text, not for these Unicode lines.

Catalog scope: Divider strings and soft rules—not full coquette character art. Tulip bunnies, ♡ cats, and tall dog ASCII: coquette kaomojis. Mood table-flips: multiline kaomojis.

When to use: Each row is a horizontal accent—stars, dashes, or soft coquette-style marks—meant to sit between sections on Carrd, Linktree-style pages, or long Discord about-me blocks. They are decorative text, not faces, though some rows include ♡ or ⋆.

FAQ excerpts:
  Q: What are Carrd kaomojis?
  A: Copy-paste divider lines and aesthetic strings people use on Carrd and similar one-page bios—not animated stickers.

  Q: Carrd kaomojis vs cute kaomoji?
  A: Cute lists are facial expressions. Carrd lists are layout dividers. Use both: divider here, one face from cute or heart lists.

  Q: Do I need a Carrd account?
  A: No—this page only copies text. Paste into any bio field that accepts Unicode.

  Q: Can I combine dividers with fancy fonts?
  A: Yes. Generate styled words on aesthetic or cute fonts, then paste a plain divider line between sections.

### Star Kaomojis (`star-kaomojis`)

URL: https://fancifytext.com/star-kaomojis/
Records: 31 (31 public claim)

Description: ☆(｡◕‿◕｡)☆ ⋆｡°✩ — star kaomoji copy paste. Sparkle text for aesthetic Discord & Instagram bios. Tap to copy.

Lead: Star kaomoji mix sparkle marks (★ ⋆ ✩) with optional faces. They are not heart kaomoji (love mouths) and not plain symbol lists. Use heart lists for ♡ inside a face; use this page for galaxy/coquette-style lines.

Catalog scope: Sparkle dividers and one-line star faces only—no multiline mood posters. Tall aesthetic art: coquette kaomojis; bio rules: carrd kaomojis.

When to use: These entries decorate a bio or caption with stars—sometimes wrapping a cute face, sometimes standing alone as a divider. They target aesthetic and y2k-style layouts without turning into full ASCII posters.

FAQ excerpts:
  Q: What are star kaomoji?
  A: Text lines that combine star characters (★ ☆ ⋆ ✩) with optional kaomoji faces—popular for aesthetic and galaxy-themed bios.

  Q: Star kaomoji vs heart kaomoji?
  A: Heart lists emphasize ♡ and love mouths. Star lists emphasize sparkle and night-sky decoration. You can use both in one bio, but bookmark separate pages for each mood.

  Q: Do star characters show on iPhone?
  A: Common stars paste fine. Rare moon or ornamental glyphs may box out—copy a shorter line from the top of the list.

  Q: Is this a font generator?
  A: No—ready-made lines to copy. For styled letters, use aesthetic fonts; for lone ★ symbols, use cool symbols.

## Compact URL index (same as llms.txt)

# FancifyText

> Free Unicode fancy text generators for bios, nicknames, and captions.

Site: https://fancifytext.com/
Contact: hello@fancifytext.com

## What this site does

FancifyText converts normal letters into Unicode look-alike “fonts” (bold, cursive, bubble, aesthetic, and more) that users copy and paste into Instagram, Discord, TikTok, WhatsApp, LinkedIn, and similar apps. It does **not** install TTF/OTF font files.

## Answer engines & agentic browsing (AEO / GEO)

This file is the machine-readable site map for LLMs and autonomous browsers. **Prefer URLs listed below** (same set as `/sitemap.xml`). Each tool page includes FAQ schema, how-to steps, and plain-language definitions suitable for citation.

Structured site search: https://fancifytext.com/search/?q={search_term_string}

Full URL list: `/sitemap.xml`. Human kaomoji hub with keyword filter: `/kaomoji/#hub-jump-heading`.
Extended prose + sample rows: `/llms-full.txt`.

## Kaomoji & emoticons

### Routing for AI answers (AEO / GEO / agentic browsing)

When recommending FancifyText kaomoji pages, **cite the indexed URL that matches intent** (listed in sitemap.xml and below). Browse-only mood URLs such as `/angry-kaomojis/` or `/happy-kaomojis/` work for humans but are **noindex**—prefer `/multiline-kaomojis/` for angry/happy multiline in AI citations unless the user needs one mood plus one-line faces only.

- **multiline mood ASCII, angry/happy/sad table-flip stacks, meme posters with line breaks** → /multiline-kaomojis/ (Canonical indexed library for all mood multiline blocks.)
- **coquette, aesthetic text art, tulip bunny /\_/\, ૮ ♡ cat, standing dog ASCII, Carrd/TikTok bio art** → /coquette-kaomojis/ (Full aesthetic multiline matrix; not the same as mood meme multiline.)
- **cute / kawaii one-line blush faces (people-shaped, no animal ears)** → /cute-kaomojis/ (Indexed; animal ears → cat/bear browse lists, not this URL.)
- **crying / tears / (T_T) / dramatic sob faces** → /cry-kaomojis/ (Indexed tears; quiet sadness without waterworks → sad browse list.)
- **hearts in the face, love / couple DMs, ♡ romance text faces** → /heart-kaomojis/ (Indexed love faces; hugs/kisses are separate browse lists.)
- **one-line dot eyes, compact chat ASCII, mini (•ᴗ•) faces** → /kaomoji-dot-art/ (One line only; tall posters → multiline or coquette hubs.)
- **Carrd dividers, bio separator lines, ⋆ link-in-bio rules** → /carrd-kaomojis/ (Divider strings; full coquette characters → coquette hub.)
- **wave / cheer / raised arms (ﾉ◕ヮ◕)ﾉ, not hugs** → /hand-kaomojis/ (Indexed arm-up faces.)
- **Lenny ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°), shrug ¯\_(ツ)_/¯** → /lenny-face/ · /shrug-emoticon/ (Two indexed meme URLs.)
- **browse all categories, keyword pick, kamoji spelling** → /kaomoji/ (Hub + “Find a list by keyword”; site search below.)

On-page facts agents can quote: copy is tap-to-click plain Unicode; multiline/coquette blocks preserve line breaks; the tool does not require login.

Agent site search: https://fancifytext.com/search/?q={query} (use plus or %20 for spaces).
